Using a carbide ball penetrator, and applying loads of up to 3.000 kgf, Brinell hardness tester following ASTM E-10 is widely used on castings and forgings. This method requires optical reading of the diameter of ball indentation and using a chart to convert the average measurement to Brinell hardness value. We offer low-cost handheld Brinell scopes as well as a popular line of Automatic Brinell Microscopes for a high frequency of testing. Qualitest also offers Automatic In-line hardness testers for high volume testing.

 Theory/Method
Principle of Operation
The primary function behind a Brinell Hardness Tester is incredibly straightforward. It provides an exceptionally dependable method to see exactly how much a structural component fights back when you press a solid, densely compacted ball into its outer surface. You are essentially gauging the exact physical dimensions of the permanent impression left behind.
The Application: You take a fiercely resilient ball, fabricated from heavy-duty steel or tungsten carbide, typically measuring 1 to 10 mm wide, and press it firmly into your material using a highly specific, carefully controlled amount of force. For instance, highly dependable benchtop models like our QualiBrineller™ allow you to apply precise physical loads ranging from 62.5 kgf up to 3,000 kgf.
The Dwell: You keep that steady pressure going for a set duration, generally 10 to 15 seconds for various steel types.
The Measurement: Once you pull the heavy weight away, you are left with a circular mark. You measure how wide that mark is across two different directions, average those two numbers out, and that gives you your official "Brinell Hardness Number," guaranteeing you meet strict ASTM E-10 and ISO 6506 international standards.
Standard Testing Parameters (Example: Wood Flooring/Soft Metals)
Ball Width: 10 mm
Total Force: 30 kgf (roughly 294 N)
Wait Time: 60 seconds
Report Format: HB 10/294.2/60
Theoretical Foundation
Essentially, a Brinell Hardness Tester shows us exactly how a material prefers to stretch out or physically yield before it experiences a permanent change in shape. It provides a clear look into how the deep internal structure of the metal or wood handles a heavy physical hit. 
The way the substance bunches up or dips down around that ball tells a specific story about the material's actual day-to-day strength. Because the size of the mark changes depending on how hard you press, you have to maintain your exact operational parameters without fail every single time to get high-quality, completely dependable data.
Whether you are running checks in a highly controlled laboratory setting or testing massive pipes out in the field with a portable hammer-strike option like the Telebrineller System, that strict relationship between the applied force and the resulting dent remains entirely consistent.
Advanced Testing Capabilities
In earlier days, technicians had to squint through basic magnifying glasses to guess exactly where the outer edge of the dent was, which often led to frustrating variations in results. Today, moving past that old-fashioned "guess-the-width" method means using a modern Brinell Hardness Tester is exceptionally precise.
Optical Scanning Tools
We use highly advanced digital measurement tools like the QualiScope™ II Plus and our BrinScan optical scanning series. These setups utilize high-definition CCD cameras and intelligent image-processing software to pinpoint the exact, scientifically accurate spot where the dent begins to drop off. This completely gets rid of the need to rely on subjective human guesswork.
Automated Processing
If you want to stop running every single step by hand, an updated system like the fully automatic QBrin3000™-Auto manages the loading, the waiting, and the measuring completely automatically. 
For high-volume manufacturing floors processing massive industrial parts like train wheels, automated inline solutions such as the BRE-AUT Series take over the entire repetitive testing cycle, effortlessly cutting out human mistakes.
Portable Solutions
You don't always have the luxury of dragging your massive steel plates directly into the lab. Portable units like the QualiMag™ Auto-B attach magnetically right onto the testing surface, successfully running a complete, fully automatic test cycle in roughly 16 seconds without sacrificing a single drop of testing accuracy.
Operational Considerations
If you want to extract highly dependable, brutally honest information from your Brinell Hardness Tester, you have to stick to a few heavily established professional standards. By following these straightforward rules, the testing gear we build at Worldoftest ensures you get the exact data you need without experiencing any unnecessary stress.
Surface Preparation
Ensure your test piece sits perfectly flat and remains totally free of any messy, interfering debris. If the surface is heavily rusted, roughly milled, or severely ground, your final test results can completely suffer. 
To bypass this issue entirely, highly automated setups like our Radial Arm (EF3000) and Portal Bridge Gantry (EP-3000) machines actually feature integrated surface milling tools. They prep the surface, make the indentation, and securely read the results all in one smooth operational cycle.
Friction Factors
Sometimes, the ball rubs aggressively against the material in a way that makes the item look slightly tougher than it actually is, usually inflating the final number by about 3%. Keep this minor detail in mind when you are closely reviewing your final figures.
Versatility and Adaptability
For uniquely shaped or hard-to-reach commercial components, finding the absolute right testing angle is crucial. Using highly adaptable gear, ranging from the Motorized QHB-3000E with its convenient hydraulic lifting stand to the entirely wireless E-Dynatest, ensures you can reliably capture those elastic spring-back measurements no matter what kind of soft, yielding materials or massive metal forgings you are actively trying to evaluate.
